A.name: Explorable Briefing
A.template:
## 1. Role and output

You are a senior creative technologist building a **customer-specific explorable 3D executive briefing** for a Cisco account team. It is one web page the audience can explore by themselves or be walked through: a live 3D scene in the middle, glass panels around it, and a short guided story. It is **not** a slide deck, a narrated film or a talk-track player. Do not add a presenter camera box, voice-over, slide counter or scene-by-scene deck navigation.

**Stack (use these exactly):**
- Vite 8 (`vite@8.x`) with `vite-plugin-singlefile@2.x`. Vanilla ES modules; no React, Vue or CSS framework.
- `three@0.186.0`: `WebGLRenderer`, `PerspectiveCamera`, `OrbitControls` from `three/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js`. No post-processing passes. Fake glow with additive radial-gradient sprites.
- `topojson-client@3.1.0` plus an embedded us-atlas or world-atlas topojson for the map (inline it as a JS module; never fetch at runtime).
- Every text label in 3D is a `CanvasTexture` sprite drawn at runtime; no image files.
- Font stack: `Inter, "Segoe UI", system-ui, -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Roboto, "Noto Sans", Ubuntu, Cantarell, "Helvetica Neue", sans-serif`. Do not load web fonts.

**Output:** one self-contained HTML file, `dist/{{FILE_SLUG}}.html`, under 1.2 MB, that works over `file://` with no network calls. Keep the source project in `app/` with `src/data/content.js` (all copy and data), `src/data/geo.js` (geometry), `src/three/sprites.js` (glow, label, flow, box, cylinder, camera fly, seeded RNG), `src/three/mapScene.js`, `src/three/{{SITE_KEY}}Scene.js`, `src/style.css` and `src/main.js` (UI and state). Copy and data live only in `content.js`, so the account team can edit text without touching the scene code.

Time budget: about {{HOURS}} hours in total, with roughly 30% for research, 50% for the build and 20% for review.

## 2. Customer and audience

- **Customer:** {{CUSTOMER}}, operating in {{WHERE}}.
- **Audience:** {{AUDIENCE}}. They will open the link before or after a meeting and explore on their own, or {{PRESENTER}} will drive it live on a big screen.
- **Goal of the briefing:** {{GOAL}}
- **Cisco topic:** {{SCENARIO}}
- **Cisco technologies to feature:** {{KEY_ITEMS}}
- **SIEM:** {{SIEM}}. If the customer's use of it is not publicly confirmed, label it "(assumed SIEM)" everywhere it appears and say so in Assumptions.
- **Brand line:** "Cisco for {{CUSTOMER}}" over the subtitle "{{TAGLINE}}".
- **Intro headline:** two short parallel sentences; the second gets the gradient. Example shape: "Every bungalow, a sensor. / Every mile, assured." Write one that fits {{SITE}}.

## 3. Research and the data model to fill

Research public sources first: annual report or 10-K, investor deck, the customer's newsroom, regulators and advisories for the sector, Cisco data sheets and release notes, and {{SIEM}} connector documentation. Record every source with a title, URL and group. Use only facts you can cite. Anything you invent (personas, site layout, KPIs, scenario narratives) must be labeled MODELED or ILLUSTRATIVE.

Fill these collections in `src/data/content.js`:

```js
export const BRAND = { title, subtitle, docTitle, kicker, headline: [line1, line2], intro, note, siem: '{{SIEM}}', researched: 'Month YYYY' };

// 30 to 50 sources, keyed. group is one of: '{{CUSTOMER}}', '<Industry> and <safety system>', 'Regulatory and threat', 'Cisco', '{{SIEM}}'
export const SOURCES = { key: { title, url, group } };

// 10 to 14 plain-language strings: audience, who is named and why, modeled personas, schematic geometry,
// modeled site, SIEM assumption, which integrations are documented, product availability dates,
// software release prerequisites, KPI disclaimer, threat composites, "no sensitive security information".
export const ASSUMPTIONS = [ '...' ];

// 10 to 16 places on the map. kind: hq | ops | dc | yard | project | event | site
export const PLACES = [{ id, name, sub /* address or 1-line role */, ll: [lon, lat], kind, modeled: false, src: ['key'],
  body /* 2 to 3 sourced sentences */, personas: ['id'] }];

// 6 to 8 personas: 1 to 2 PUBLIC executives (named only if sources agree, otherwise by role), the rest MODELED composites.
export const PERSONAS = [{ id, name /* "Dana, Train Dispatcher" */, role /* include "(modeled persona)" when modeled */,
  place: 'placeId', public: true|false, src: [], color: '#hex',
  priority /* one first-person line, shown as an illustrative priority, never as a quote */,
  cares: ['3 to 4 bullets'], scenarios: ['scenarioId'] }];

// 7 to 9 technologies, one of which is {{SIEM}} itself.
export const TECH = [{ id, abbr /* 2 to 3 letters */, name, short, color: '#hex', obj /* site object or control-plane id */,
  src: [], facts: ['4 to 5 verified facts with numbers'], wayside /* where it sits in {{SITE}}, 1 sentence */,
  sentinel /* the documented path into {{SIEM}}, or "integration pattern to validate" */, scenarios: [] }];

// Exactly 8 scenarios (see section 8).
export const SCENARIOS = [{ id, title, focus /* site pose id */, place /* map place id */, personas: [], tech: [],
  hook, without: ['4 steps'], with: ['4 steps'],
  kpi: { without: { mttd, vis, roll }, with: { mttd, vis, roll } } }];

// Exactly 7 story steps (see section 7).
export const STORY = [{ title, view: 'map'|'{{SITE_KEY}}', place: 'id'|null, focus: 'poseId', mode: 'without'|'with'|'split', open: 'type:id'|null, text, src: [] }];

export const LEGEND = { map: [['sw'|'ln', '#hex', 'label']], mapNote, site: [...], siteNote };
```

In `src/data/geo.js`: the map projection origin, the telemetry hub `{{HUB}}` as `[lon, lat]`, the list of highlighted regions (the states or countries where {{CUSTOMER}} operates, from a source), 15 to 25 schematic corridors or links as `{ name, coords: [[lon,lat],...], main?: true, special?: 'eventId' }` drawn between real city coordinates, and the topojson for {{MAP_REGION}}.

## 4. Layout spec (desktop 1440x900; must also work at 1280x720)

- **Canvas:** fixed and full-bleed behind everything.
- **Top bar** `#top`: fixed, 64px tall, padding 0 18px, gap 18px, flex; background `linear-gradient(rgba(3,8,20,.95), rgba(3,8,20,.55))` with a 1px bottom line. From left: brand block (Cisco 7-bar logo, title 16px/700, subtitle 12px muted, min-width 230px); a **view** segmented control "Network map | {{SITE_LABEL}}"; a **mode** segmented control "Without Cisco | With Cisco | Split view"; then, pushed right, the buttons **Guided story** (primary), **Sources** and **Assumptions**.
- **Left navigator** `#nav`: glass, `left:14px; top:78px; bottom:150px; width:300px`. A 4-column tab row (Personas, Technology, Scenarios, Places) over a scrolling list of items: a 34px rounded-square color dot with initials or an index, the title plus a badge, and a muted sub line.
- **Right detail panel** `#detail`: glass, `right:14px; top:78px; bottom:150px; width:400px; padding:18px 20px`, scrolls. Hidden (opacity 0, shifted 20px right, no pointer events) until something is selected.
- **Legend** `#legend`: glass, `left:330px; bottom:150px; max-width:280px`, 11.5px rows with 10px dots or 18x3 line swatches and a one-line hint. Content changes with the view.
- **Story dock** `#story`: glass, centred at `bottom:16px`, `width:min(900px, 100vw - 40px)`, padding 12px 14px: a round prev button (38px), the body (step number "3 / 7" in cyan 11px/800, title 15px/700, text 13px with inline source links, and 7 progress bars 22x4), a play/pause button and a next button.
- **Split overlay:** a vertical gradient divider at 50% and two pills, "WITHOUT CISCO" (red) left of centre and "WITH CISCO" (teal) right of centre, at the top of the scene.
- **Intro overlay:** full screen, `radial-gradient(at 30% 40%, rgba(4,159,217,.18), rgba(2,6,15,.9) 60%)`, a content block (max 760px): the kicker, the 2-line h1 (`clamp(34px,5vw,58px)`), a paragraph (16px/1.6), two big buttons "Start the guided story" (primary) and "Explore freely", and a small honesty note.
- **Modal:** dimmed full screen, a glass box `min(900px,92vw)`, max 84vh, scrolls, with an X close button.
- At 1200px and below: detail 340px, nav 260px, legend left 290px. In split mode (and on the H key) add `body.collapsed`: the nav slides off left, the legend hides, and the detail narrows to 330px.
- **Mobile (760px and below):** the top bar wraps to two rows (brand, Browse and Guided story on row 1; both segmented controls on a horizontally scrollable row 2); Sources and Assumptions move into the Browse sheet or stay reachable; the nav becomes a full-width sheet opened by "Browse"; the detail becomes a bottom sheet (max 50vh, close button) above the dock; the legend hides; the scenario columns stack. No horizontal overflow at 390px.

## 5. Visual design tokens

```css
:root{ --bg:#050a16; --glass:#0a1224c7; --line:#78aaff2e; --text:#e6eefc; --muted:#93a4c3;
       --cisco:#049fd9; --good:#2dd4bf; --bad:#f87171; --ms:#60a5fa; }
.glass{ background:var(--glass); border:1px solid var(--line); border-radius:16px; box-shadow:0 10px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.45); }
```
- No backdrop blur; the 78% fill lets the 3D show through.
- Buttons: radius 10, `rgba(255,255,255,.06)` fill, 1px `--line` border, 13px/600. Primary: `linear-gradient(135deg,#049fd9,#0369a1)`. Hover: `brightness(1.15)`.
- Segmented control: radius 12 track, radius 9 buttons. The active state is cyan (`rgba(4,159,217,.22)` plus an inset ring at .6); "Without" active is red (`rgba(248,113,113,.2)`, ring .7); "With" active is teal (`rgba(45,212,191,.2)`, ring .7).
- Badges (9.5px/800, letter-spacing .08em, radius 6): PUBLIC `#7dd3fc` on `rgba(56,189,248,.18)`; MODELED and ILLUSTRATIVE `#fde047` on `rgba(250,204,21,.16)`.
- Section headings in the detail: 11px uppercase, letter-spacing .12em, muted. h2 21px. Body 13.5px/1.5. Chips: pills with radius 999.
- Without and With columns: red and teal tinted cards (.08 fill, .35 border). The column that does not match the current mode drops to opacity .45.
- KPI tiles: 3 across, radius 10, muted label, value line "red → teal".
- SIEM box: blue `rgba(37,99,235,.12)` fill, `rgba(96,165,250,.45)` border, an 11px uppercase header with the SIEM's logo mark built in CSS (no image).
- Priority block: 3px cyan left border, italic 14px, with an "Illustrative priority, not a quote" label above it.
- Category colors on the map: hq `#38bdf8`, ops `#f59e0b`, dc `#06b6d4`, yard or terminal `#facc15`, project `#a78bfa`, event `#f43f5e`, site `#22c55e`; corridors `#f5b301`; Without red `#ef4444`; With teal `#2dd4bf` and `#22d3ee`; SIEM flows `#93c5fd`.

## 6. 3D scene spec

**Renderer:** antialias, `preserveDrawingBuffer:true`, pixel ratio capped at 2, sRGB output, ACES filmic tone mapping at exposure 1.1, PCF shadows. One canvas and two `Scene`s; only the active view renders. Camera: perspective, fov 45 (60 in split), near .1, far 500. OrbitControls with damping .08, `maxPolarAngle .47*PI`, distance 2 to 80. Camera moves use a custom 1.4 to 1.6 s cubic in-out fly with an arcing lift; switching views fades through black (.45 s).

**Network map view ({{MAP_REGION}}):** background and FogExp2 `#050a16`, hemisphere plus one directional light, a dark ground plane and a faint 200x200 grid. Project lon/lat equirectangularly scaled by cos(latitude). Extrude the regions where {{CUSTOMER}} operates (depth .16, deep blue with emissive, bright blue outlines) and the others flat and dark. Draw corridors as Catmull-Rom tubes with an additive halo, plus small gold glow "trains" moving along them; draw one special event corridor in rose. Places: a glowing vertical pin (taller for HQ), a ground ring and a top glow in the kind color, plus a canvas label (larger with a sub line for HQ and events), and an invisible sphere as the raycast target. Hover shows a tooltip; click selects; the selected ring pulses larger and the other labels dim.
- **Without:** sample points every ~1.1 units along all corridors as pulsing red rings, with a "?" label on every 4th: unmonitored sites.
- **With:** the same points as teal glows; every 3rd sends an arched additive flow with a moving bead to {{HUB}}, where a large pulsing glow sits.

**Site view ({{SITE}}, a modeled diorama):** a dusk palette (background `#0a1424`, linear fog 45 to 110), a warm shadow-casting key light, a cool fill and a hemisphere light; ground, infrastructure and seeded-random scenery. Build 6 to 8 named field assets that matter to {{CUSTOMER}} ({{SITE_ASSETS}}), an equipment enclosure with a visible rack, primary and secondary backhaul (wired path plus a carrier tower), and one moving element that drives state (for rail, a train that sets signal aspects and lowers crossing gates; for other sectors, a comparable process such as a conveyor, a vehicle, a pump cycle or a crane). Every asset gets a canvas label with a sub line and a named camera pose.
- **Without layer:** a legacy kit in the rack with red labels, an intruder figure, 3 red threat flows from off-site, and 5 pulsing red "?" callouts naming the blind spots.
- **With layer:** Cisco kit in the rack with lit bezels and blinking port LEDs, a translucent sensor dome with a wireframe, teal rings at each asset, 6 to 8 floating "control plane" labels (one per featured product, plus {{SIEM}} in deep blue), colored bead flows from the edge devices to the products and on to {{SIEM}}, a path-assurance flow along the backhaul with hop glows, and 3 green callouts naming what is now known.
- **Highlight:** a white pulsing ring and glow at the focused asset; other control-plane labels fade to .45.

**Split mode:** render the active scene twice per frame with the scissor test: the left half in Without and the right half in With, each with aspect `w/2/h`. Map raycasting must account for the half the pointer is in.

## 7. Interactions and deep links

- **Intro:** "Start the guided story" goes to step 1 and autoplays. "Explore freely" flies to the overview and sets the dock to "Explore" with a how-to line.
- **Tabs** switch the list. Selecting an item opens its detail, highlights it in the list, and switches the tab to the item's type. A place flies the map to it; a persona flies to its place; a technology switches to With, opens the site view, and highlights and flies to its object; a scenario opens the site view at its focus.
- **Detail chips** cross-link persona, scenario, technology and place. A scenario has three CTA buttons (Show without, Show with, Split view). A place has "Enter {{SITE_LABEL}}".
- **Guided story:** exactly 7 steps. (1) Who {{CUSTOMER}} is, in numbers (map overview). (2) The pressure: an event or a growth project (map, place). (3) Regulators and adversaries (map, HQ). (4) Inside {{SITE}} (site overview). (5) Without Cisco: blind, flat, slow (site, focus on the enclosure, opens the lead scenario). (6) With Cisco: every site is a sensor (With mode, opens the key sensing technology). (7) Side by side (Split mode, opens a second scenario). Steps 1 to 3 force Without. The dots fill up to the current step and are clickable. Play advances every 7.5 s and stops at the end; any manual action stops play.
- **Keyboard:** Left and Right arrows step the story, Esc closes the modal (and the mobile sheet), H toggles the collapsed panels.
- **Hash deep links** (read on load and on `hashchange`; any parameter skips the intro): `mode=without|with|split`, `open=persona:<id>|tech:<id>|scenario:<id>|place:<id>`, `view=map|{{SITE_KEY}}` with optional `focus=<pose>`, `story=0..6`. Write the hash back with `history.replaceState` as the state changes, keeping colons readable.
- **Sources modal:** an intro line ("Public sources used for facts in this app (researched <month year>). Items labeled MODELED or ILLUSTRATIVE are not sourced {{CUSTOMER}} facts."), then an h3 per group and an ordered list of title plus URL. **Assumptions modal:** an ordered list plus a badge legend.

## 8. Scenario authoring rules

Write exactly 8 scenarios across security, operations and resilience. They must match the topic, {{SCENARIO}}, and include at least: an unknown device on the OT edge, a backhaul or path failure, configuration drift or stale firmware, a disaster rebuild or major event, IT-to-OT lateral movement, third-party or vendor remote access, a safety-critical field asset, and regulatory evidence for the board.
- **Title:** concrete and visual, 4 to 7 words.
- **Hook:** one sentence situation in the field.
- **Without (4 steps):** what the people actually see and do today, ending in delay, a truck roll or late discovery. No product names. No mockery of the customer's current vendors.
- **With (4 steps):** each step is product, action, result, using only capabilities from that product's verified facts. One step must name the documented path into {{SIEM}} (connector, syslog/CEF via the agent, webhook, or a native export). If no documented path exists, write "integration pattern to validate".
- **KPIs:** three short contrasts (time to detect, visibility, field impact), for example "Weeks" to "Minutes". They are modeled; never present them as measured.
- Tie each scenario to 2 to 3 personas, 3 to 5 technologies, one map place and one site focus pose.

## 9. Labeling and assumptions

- Every persona and place shows PUBLIC or MODELED; every scenario shows ILLUSTRATIVE; KPI blocks are titled "Outcome (modeled KPIs)".
- Each detail panel ends with a Sources block of links, or "Modeled content, no external source."
- Named executives: never invent quotes. Show their line as "Illustrative priority, not a quote". If sources conflict on a name, show the role only and explain in Assumptions.
- Map lines are "schematic, modeled"; the site is "Representative site, modeled layout".
- Do not depict real security weaknesses of {{CUSTOMER}} or any sensitive security information. Threat scenarios are composites informed by public advisories.

## 10. Quality checks and review

1. `npm run build` produces one HTML file; open it over `file://`. There must be no console errors or warnings.
2. With Playwright (`chromium.launch({args:['--use-gl=angle','--use-angle=swiftshader','--enable-unsafe-swiftshader']})`), screenshot at 1280x720 and 1440x900: the intro, the map in Without, `#story=2`, `#view={{SITE_KEY}}&mode=with`, `#mode=split&open=scenario:<lead>`, `#open=persona:<exec>` and `#open=tech:<sensor>`. Also screenshot the home state at 390x844. Look at every image.
3. Check: no label collisions over the panels at the overview poses; the detail never covers the active asset; the split pills are readable; `scrollWidth == innerWidth` on mobile.
4. Click through every tab item and every chip once; step the whole story with the arrow keys; open both modals; confirm that each hash restores its state after a reload.
5. Fact pass: every number in PLACES, TECH facts and STORY has a source key that resolves; every MODELED item says so.
6. Do 2 to 3 fix-and-review passes on layout, color, spacing and motion.

## 11. Deliverables

- `dist/{{FILE_SLUG}}.html`: the single-file app.
- `app/`: the Vite source (package.json pinned to the versions above).
- `shots/`: the review screenshots.
- A short README: how to run and build it, how to edit `content.js`, the deep-link list, and the open assumptions to confirm with {{CUSTOMER}} (especially the {{SIEM}} assumption).

B.template:
## 1. Role and output
Use the cisco-3d-stage skill (read its SKILL.md and every file in references/ before writing code). Build an interactive 3D stage presentation from the skill's starter: a Three.js r170 web app with vendored Three.js, Inter and JetBrains Mono, plain ES modules and no build step. It moves like a slide deck: right arrow, Space, Enter and left click step through animations; up and down skip whole scenes; every scene is its own lit 3D world reached by a 1.9 second camera flight. Deliver two editions of the same deck: the presenter edition, and the narrated film edition (body attribute data-edition="narrated") with pre-rendered neural voices and the animated AI narrator. Presenter: {{PRESENTER}}.

## 2. The talk
Title: {{TALK_TITLE}}. Audience: {{AUDIENCE}}. The one change I want in the room: {{GOAL}}. Length: {{MINUTES}} minutes, about 150 spoken words per minute, so plan the scene count and clicks from that (a 20 minute talk is about 3,000 words of notes, 15 to 20 scenes, 50 to 60 clicks). Group scenes into chapters and number every eyebrow with its chapter: "00 · Prologue", "01 · The shift", "03 · The method".

## 3. Story arc
Shape the talk the way the FutureSE talk "A spoken word away" was shaped, adapted to this topic:
1. Prologue, hero layout: the bridge bars rise; one headline that names the change.
2. The shift (2 scenes): what the audience does today and why it stops working. Use the "old medium breaks" recipe (a wall of flat frames that tilt, wobble, then fold into a sphere) and a "search versus brief" style contrast if the topic has a before and after way of working.
3. The flip (2 scenes): a pyramid that balances on its point, flips onto a solid base, and lights tier by tier. Use it for the structural insight of the talk.
4. The method (1 scene, focus layout): the structure underneath, one numbered block per click, each with a block color, a heading, a quoted fragment in mono and a one-line explanation. Method blocks: {{METHOD_BLOCKS}}.
5. The examples (one scene each, world-and-screen recipe): a diorama of each example's real world beside a glass browser screen that steps through captures, with a live link button for each. Examples and links: {{EXAMPLES}}. Before them, a lineage galaxy scene shows the examples as glowing nodes on a spiral, joined by arcs in the order they were built.
6. Workshop ({{WORKSHOP}}): workshop layout; the audience fills a short brief, the 3D base slabs light as they type, a 10 minute timer appears, and the finished prompt copies with one click. The narrated film pauses here.
7. The loop and the guardrails (2 scenes): what keeps the method honest (loop recipe with documents flowing around a ring; hex shields that light two per click).
8. Epilogue, hero layout: bridge bars return over an audio-wave floor; the closing line.

Cisco content to weave through the examples and the flip: {{SCENARIO}}. It must include: {{KEY_ITEMS}}.

## 4. Scene authoring rules
- Write all copy in js/content.js. For every scene: id, eyebrow, title (a statement), grad (the outcome clause in the gradient), lead (one sentence), beats (one per click, each { h, p } and short), notes (one paragraph per click, written to be spoken, "Click." marks a new step, 25 to 80 words), optional layout (hero, focus, workshop, or the default stack), optional prompt chips ([[blockKey, text], ...] under the heading "Prompt logic"), optional verse: true for live links.
- One idea per scene, one change per click. Step 0 is the establishing shot. Every click changes the world, not just the text.
- Design one world per scene in js/scenes.js with the skill's kit (wireBox, gridFloor, person, plane, points, drawTube, arc, label, canvasPanel, glowSprite, mediaScreen, worldScene). The world must mean something for its scene: model the example's real, public layout where you can (terminals and concourses, hospital floors, a branch map) and label modeled data as modeled.
- Give every scene a sky (bg colors a, b, c and a mix of aurora, horizon grid, data rain, starfield) and a particle formation in js/particles.js. Adjacent scenes never share either. Turn the sky with the story through bgSteps: red or amber for the problem, blue or green after the fix.
- Mix layouts so the rhythm changes. Keep text off bright geometry with the left scrim, the view offset and diorama scale.

## 5. Presenter tooling
Keep everything the skill ships: presenter window (P), off-camera talking points window (T) with the pace clock, notes drawer (N), scene menu (M), camera box bottom right with the presenter's name tag, live link buttons (L), clean mode (H), printable talk track (?talktrack) and #scene/step deep links. Write POINTS in js/script.js: 1 to 3 bullets of 3 to 9 words per click, the names, numbers and the one phrase to land. Keep notes, beats, POINTS and NARRATION the same length for every scene.

## 6. Narrated edition
Write NARRATION in js/script.js, one paragraph per click at 150 to 170 words per minute, in the third person. The narrator opens by saying it is an AI narrator standing in for {{PRESENTER_NAME}} and never impersonates them. Name the pause at the workshop ("The film will pause here. Press play when you are ready."). Render Ava, Andrew, Emma and Brian with tools/gen_audio.py (edge-tts), build the copy with tools/sync_narrated.sh, and serve it with a range-capable server so the scrubber can seek. The film offers device voice and captions only as fallbacks.

## 7. Design rules
Follow the skill's design system exactly: midnight #050e1d ground, blue #00bceb accent, green #6cc04a outcome, amber and red only for problem states, the headline gradient #7fe3ff to #00bceb to #6cc04a on the outcome clause, Inter (CiscoSansTT first in the stack) and JetBrains Mono, glass panels rgba(7,24,45,0.82) with a 1px line border and 18px radius. Labels, panels and screenshots go on the OVERLAY layer after bloom so they stay crisp. Never use em dashes anywhere. {{BRAND_RULES}}

## 8. Research and truth
Research each example and the Cisco content in public sources first. Cite them in a sources list that the printable talk track shows. Customer names and links exactly as given. Facts are accurate or labelled modeled; no invented quotes or figures. Media screens show real captures of each build (1280x720 JPG, optional 6 to 12 second muted MP4); if you cannot capture one, draw it and label it as an illustration.

## 9. Way of working
Follow the operating rules at the top of this prompt. A complete, reviewed deck beats an ambitious unfinished one.

## 10. Review
Run tools/review.mjs at 1440x900, 1280x720 and 390x844 and open every screenshot. Fix text over bright geometry, empty frames, edge-on labels, screens off frame and overflow at 390px. Test arrow keys, clicks, up and down, Home and End, deep links, presenter and talking points sync, and the film flow (play, auto-advance, workshop pause, end card). No console errors. Grep for em and en dashes; there must be none.

## 11. Deliverables
Both editions, TALKING_POINTS.md, SCRIPT.md with the runtime of each voice, and TALK_TRACK.md from tools/gen_docs.mjs. {{PUBLISHING}}

# Build a Leadership Digital Twin briefing page for {{CUSTOMER}}

## 1. Role and output

You are a senior creative technologist on a Cisco and Splunk account team. Build ONE long-scrolling web page: an IT leadership briefing for {{CUSTOMER}} with a live 3D "digital twin" of its territory as the hero. It is a **leave-behind page that people scroll and read**. It is not a slide deck.

Do not build any of the following:
- slide or step navigation;
- a presenter camera box;
- a narrated talk-track HUD;
- keyboard-driven scenes.

**Stack (use exactly this):**
- Vite 5 with vanilla ES modules: no React and no UI framework. Build the DOM from template strings plus a tiny `el(tag, cls, text)` helper.
- **Three.js r169** (`three@0.169.0`) for the twin, loaded through a dynamic `import('./scene.js')` so it stays a separate module. Use these addons: `CSS2DRenderer` for labels, and `EffectComposer` + `RenderPass` + `UnrealBloomPass` + `OutputPass` for glow.
- Fonts: `@fontsource/inter` in weights 400, 500, 600, 700 and 800.
- Output: `vite-plugin-singlefile`, so `npm run build` emits **one self-contained `dist/index.html`** with JS, CSS and fonts inlined. Copy it to the deliverable name in section 11. It must open from `file://` with no network.
- Guard WebGL with `getContext('webgl2')||getContext('webgl')`. Without WebGL, show "WebGL is not available in this browser. The brief below is fully readable." in place of the canvas.
- Pause the render loop with an `IntersectionObserver` once the hero is off screen.

Time budget: about {{HOURS}} hours across research, build and review. Spend roughly a third of it on research and citations.

## 2. Customer and leadership audience

- **Customer:** {{CUSTOMER}}
- **Territory shown on the twin:** {{WHERE}}
- **Audience:** {{AUDIENCE}}
- **What the page must achieve:** {{GOAL}}
- **Cisco and Splunk topic:** {{SCENARIO}}
- **Platform they already run:** {{PLATFORM_OWNED}}. Treat it as the base everything builds on. Mark it "in place" everywhere.
- **Current joint work:** {{CURRENT_WORK}}
- **Regulatory frame:** {{REGULATORY_FRAME}}
- **Catalysts (merger, build-out, deadlines):** {{CATALYSTS}}
- **Mission or critical customers they serve:** {{MISSION_CUSTOMERS}}
- **Sites and functions to place on the twin:** {{KEY_ITEMS}}
- **Departments to cover:** {{DEPARTMENTS}}
- **Prepared by / date line:** {{PRESENTER}}, {{BRIEFING_DATE}}

Write for CIO and CISO staff. Use second person ("your teams", "the platform you already run"). Keep sentences short and concrete with numbers. Lead with outcomes, not products.

## 3. Research plan and citation rules

1. **Collect 40–70 public sources.** Draw on the customer's 10-K/10-Q/8-K, earnings-call transcripts, investor decks, regulator dockets, press releases, project sites, sector threat reports (Dragos, E-ISAC, CISA, vendor CTI), the regulation's text, and Cisco and Splunk product docs and launch posts.
   - Store each source as `{id:'s1', org, date, title, url}`.
   - Note today's research cut-off date in the method notes.
2. **Extract:** 6 headline KPIs; 12 strategic initiatives, each with its evidence; 12 sector threats; the regulatory requirements; the customer's own security operating model; production AI use; and any federal or critical-customer relationships.
3. **Citations:**
   - Every number, date and named fact about the customer or the sector gets a citation chip after the claim. The chip shows the source's ordinal number (array index + 1), links to `#src-sN`, and its `title` is the source title.
   - Never invent a source or a URL. If you cannot source a fact, cut it.
4. **Provenance labels.** Use exactly three, and never blur them:
   - `Public sources`: cited;
   - `Our work together`: account context from {{CURRENT_WORK}}, not cited;
   - `Our recommendation`: guidance.
5. **Threats are sector patterns.** The Threats lede must state: "Nothing here implies an incident at {{CUSTOMER}}."
6. **Dashboards are illustrative.** Tag every one "Illustrative data". A value may be called "reported" only if it is cited.
7. **Classify every use case and play against what the customer owns:**
   - "New use case on what you already run": all products are owned;
   - "Extends what you run": some are owned;
   - "New capability": none are.

   Show the totals in the Story section.
8. Hedge authorization and availability (FedRAMP, IL levels, regional support) with a "confirmed during design" caveat.

## 4. Page anatomy, section by section

**Sticky top bar.**
- Lockup: Cisco bars-logo SVG | `splunk>` with "a Cisco company" | **{{CUSTOMER}}** with "IT leadership briefing".
- Then 12 anchor links: Digital Twin, For IT Leadership, Our Work Together, Story, Alignment, Threats, Departments, Dashboards, Cloud Control, Federal (rename it to fit {{MISSION_CUSTOMERS}}), Roadmap, Sources.
- Style it as glass (`rgba(2,7,16,.86)` with a 14 px blur) at 60 px tall.
- On mobile the nav becomes a horizontally scrollable row. The page itself must never scroll sideways.

**0. Hero `#twin` (100vh, min 680 px).** A full-bleed canvas behind a left rail about 540 px wide. The rail holds:
1. A cyan kicker, "PREPARED FOR {{CUSTOMER}} IT LEADERSHIP, {{BRIEFING_DATE}}".
2. The H1 in three runs: "{{CUSTOMER}}," in white, then **"operated by agents,"** in a cyan gradient, then **"grounded in one data fabric"** in a magenta-to-orange gradient that spans the wrapped lines.
3. A two-sentence lede ending "Click any site, or press play to walk the story."
4. The "Listen to the security briefing / N minute narrated overview" button.
5. A **3×2 KPI grid**.
6. The **story card**, pinned at the bottom of the rail.

Elsewhere on the hero:
- Top right: layer chips (All layers, Operations, + Splunk fabric, + Cloud Control) with a red-outlined "Simulate attacks" toggle below them.
- A right-side asset drawer that opens when a site is clicked.
- Bottom right: the legend strip (territory, transmission, Splunk ingest, agent actions, threat path).
- Bottom center: "Scroll for the full brief".

## 5. The hex twin

- **Projection:** an equirectangular projection centered on {{WHERE}}: `x=(lon-lon0)*k*cos(lat0)`, `z=(lat0-lat)*k`. Choose `k` so the territory spans about 50 world units. North points away from the start camera.
- **Territory:**
  - Hand-trace a simplified polygon of 15–30 vertices for each state or region in {{WHERE}}.
  - Fill the polygons with a pointy-top hex lattice of radius about 0.9 and render it as one `InstancedMesh` of short hex prisms (height 0.3–1.4, varied by noise).
  - Prism tops are near-black (#05080f) with a faint emissive rim.
  - Draw hex **edges** as a second instanced line or thin-ring mesh with additive blending, colored per region: magenta #e5007e for the core, amber #f7931e for the secondary regions, and cyan near the coast.

- **Floor:** a huge cyan square grid (`GridHelper` or a shader plane) on y = 0, fading into fog (#00243f). Light it with a cyan hemisphere light and add a bluish vertical background gradient.
- **Sites:**
  - Place one emissive sphere or beacon per entry in {{KEY_ITEMS}}, colored by department.
  - Each gets a `CSS2DObject` label: a dark pill with a colored dot and the short name. Add an italic place suffix for sites outside the territory.
  - Raycast clicks to open the asset drawer, which shows the department tag, name, function, "What the public record says" (cited facts), "Where Splunk and Cisco help", and buttons for "Personas and use cases" and "Open mock dashboard". Add a pulsing focus ring on the selected site.

- **Layers:**
  - `ops`: hexes and sites.
  - `fabric`: adds the grid floor glow, rising orange "Splunk ingest" particle streams from each site, and the callout "splunk> Cisco Data Fabric — {owned and platform products}".
  - `agentic`: adds a bright **Cloud Control core** sphere about 18 units above the territory, two tilted elliptical rings, and **8 agent orbs** orbiting slowly. Each orb has a pill label and is clickable (`onAgent`). Add sky-blue arcs from each orb to its department's site, and the callout "Cisco Cloud Control AgenticOps — AI Canvas, Agent Builder, App Builder, AI Defense, Splunk AI Agent Monitoring".

## 8. Audio briefing

1. Write a 10-chapter narration script, `story[i].say`, of 55–80 words per chapter and about 5–6 minutes in total. Use the same facts as the chapter bodies, in a spoken register with no citation numbers.
2. **The production audio is rendered offline**, one MP3 per chapter (`audio/{id}.mp3`), then concatenated into `audio/briefing.mp3` with `ffmpeg -f concat`. Render it with any of these:
   - edge-tts (`en-US-AndrewMultilingualNeural`);
   - Gemini TTS (`gemini-2.5-flash-preview-tts`);
   - ElevenLabs (multilingual v2).

   Embed small files as base64, or ship `audio/` beside the HTML.
3. **In the single-file build**, set `AUDIO_MODE='speech'`:
   - Read each chapter with `speechSynthesis`, preferring an en-US natural voice, at rate 1.0.
   - On `onend`, advance to the next chapter.
   - Estimate progress at 150 words per minute.
   - The chip says "Script" and opens a dialog with the full narration.
   - If speech is missing, "Read script" opens the same dialog.
   - Starting audio stops "Play story", and starting "Play story" stops audio.
4. "Play story" without audio advances chapters every 9 s. Each chapter calls `flyTo(cam.p, cam.t, 2.6)`, sets its layer (a `threat` chapter means `all` plus `setThreat(true)`) and selects `focus`. Once you are past chapter 0, `body.story` fades the H1, lede and KPIs so the map shows through.

## 10. Quality checks and review

- No console errors or warnings from your code. No network requests after load: fonts are inlined and there is no CDN.
- Check with Playwright at 1440×900, 1280×720 and 390×844. Launch Chromium with `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader` so WebGL renders headless. At each size:
  - take a full-page screenshot and viewport shots of the hero, the KPIs and story card, the threats, and the Cloud Control or roadmap section;
  - confirm `document.documentElement.scrollWidth <= innerWidth` (no horizontal overflow);
  - click each layer chip, Simulate attacks, a site, Play story, →, and an agent orb.
- Read your screenshots and fix layout, color, type, spacing and behavior. Do at least two passes.
- **Content audit:**
  - every number is cited;
  - every citation resolves to a list entry;
  - nothing is marked "reported" without a source;
  - the threats lede carries the no-incident line;
  - every dashboard is tagged illustrative;
  - the own-line counts in Story match the data.
- **Accessibility:**
  - every button has a name;
  - focus is visible;
  - text contrast is at least 4.5:1;
  - `prefers-reduced-motion` stops the idle drift and the ring animations.

D.name: Mission Globe
D.template:
# Type D, Mission Globe: build prompt


## 1. Role and output

You are a senior creative technologist building a **Mission Globe** for a Cisco account team: a dark, cinematic 3D globe of {{CUSTOMER}}'s real locations. Each location hosts a "mission", a weak IT signal that appears hours or days before it becomes a business problem. The viewer plays each mission twice on a scrubbable 4D timeline (traditional vs {{SCENARIO}}), makes a scored decision, and sees the modeled value protected.

Not a slide deck: no presenter camera box, no deck navigation. One globe, three modes (Present, Play, Learn), a game layer and a narrated audio dock.

**Stack (exact versions):** Vite 8.3.5, three 0.186.1 (OrbitControls, EffectComposer, RenderPass, UnrealBloomPass, OutputPass, CSS2DRenderer), gsap 3.15.0, topojson-client 3.1.0 with the Natural Earth 110m land TopoJSON inlined, and vite-plugin-singlefile 2.3.4. No other dependencies, no web fonts (`Inter, "Segoe UI", system-ui, ...`).

**Output:** `dist/{{CUSTOMER_SLUG}}.html` (one file, works from `file://`), optional `dist/audio/<voice>/<hash>.mp3`, source in `app/src/` (world, timeline, narrator, audio, game, panels, dock, main, style, `data/content.json`) and `tools/narration-lines.mjs`.

Time budget: {{HOURS}} hours, in this order: content accuracy, core loop, globe, polish.

## 2. Customer and audience

- Customer: **{{CUSTOMER}}**. Global footprint: {{WHERE}}.
- Audience: {{AUDIENCE}}. Goal of the experience: {{GOAL}}.
- Cisco story: {{SCENARIO}}. Products and capabilities to feature: {{KEY_ITEMS}}.
- The customer's public strategy, which the missions must map to: {{STRATEGY}}. Its pillars and public commitments: {{STRATEGY_PILLARS}}.
- Presenter credit, used in the intro note and the page description: {{PRESENTER}}.
- Intro headline, a short promise that ends with a full stop: {{HEADLINE}}.

## 3. Research plan (do this before writing content)

1. **Public facts only** (investor relations, 10-K, strategy material, newsroom, office list). Log a source per fact in `research.md`; no source links in the UI.
2. **Missions.** Pick {{MISSION_COUNT}} locations from {{LOCATIONS}}; for each, the business unit there, one publicly documented industry challenge, and the strategy pillar it touches.
3. **Buildings.** Address, floors and height, customer-occupied floors, neighbouring landmarks. Mark anything unverified **Illustrative**.
4. **Value modeling.** A modeled exposure per mission from public benchmarks (downtime cost per minute, breach cost, SLA credits, abandonment, slippage), about $2M to $15M, with a one-sentence basis starting "Modeled:".
5. **No internal data.** Never invent internal customer metrics.

## 4. Mission authoring rules

Write {{MISSION_COUNT}} missions (default 10), each at a different real location. Together they must cover all the business functions in {{BUSINESS_FUNCTIONS}}. Each mission has exactly 3 function "lenses". Use at least 3 regions (Americas, EMEA, Asia), because badges reward completing each region. At least one mission must be a security incident measured in minutes (`unit:'m'`); the rest use hours.

Every mission needs all of the following:
- **Identity.** A `code` (M-01 to M-NN), a short evocative `title` ("Ahead of the Storm"), a `subtitle` of "City | Business unit", a `region`, 3 `lenses`, a `pillar` (the strategy pillar it protects), an `industryChallenge` (2 sentences) and a `metricName` (the business KPI being watched).
- **Timeline numbers.** `unit`, `range:[from,to]`, `agentDetect` (negative, so the lead time is real), `agentRemediate` (still before 0), `impact: 0`, `tradDetect` and `tradRecover` (after 0), `tradDip` (0.4 to 0.85) and `agentDip` (0 to 0.06).
- **Value.** `exposure` in dollars (modeled) and an `exposureBasis` that starts with "Modeled:".
- **Blast radius.** `blast`: 2 to 6 other site IDs affected if nobody acts.
- **Signals and products.** `signals`: 5 data sources the Data Fabric joins, including at least one business or external signal. `products`: about 6 Cisco and Splunk capabilities from {{KEY_ITEMS}}.
- **Events:** about 6 agentic and 5 traditional `{t, branch, sev: info|warn|crit|good, source, text}`, one sentence each from a named actor ("Capacity Agent", "War room"). The agentic branch includes a human approval in AI Canvas.
- **Narration**, six spoken paragraphs with numbers as words: `overview` ("Mission one, City.", 4-5 sentences), `briefing`, `signal` (states the lead time), `traditional` ("Here is the traditional path."), `agentic` ("Here is the AgenticOps path."), `outcome` ("The business outcome is not a faster ticket.", ending with who to talk to).
- **Decision.** A `prompt` that ends "What do you do?". Three `options`, one each of `best`, `partial` and `poor`, each `{label, detail, quality, feedback}`. Feedback is 1 or 2 sentences of consequence. The best option is always the governed agent action with human approval.
- **KPIs.** 4 rows of `{label, traditional, agentic}`, with concrete before and after values.
- **Academy chain:** `{signal, domain, capability, kpi, outcome}`.
- **Talk track.** 3 sentences an account rep can say verbatim.
- **Discovery.** 3 open questions for the business owner, about the last bad day and its cost.
- **Quiz.** 2 items of `{q, options:[3], answer, why}`. One is about business impact, one about how the agent knew.

**Per-mission product views** (`views[missionId]`): `service`; `tree` (6 nodes) with `rootNode`; `kpis:[4 {name, unit, good, bad}]`; `path` (5 typed hops, `bad` hop index, `alt` hop, `badMetric`, `goodMetric`, `source`); `assistant {q, spl (3-line SPL2), a, rows:[3], followups:[3]}` where the last follow-up opens AI Canvas; `canvas {prompt, plan:[4 {agent, source, task}], finding {title, evidence:[3]}, action {title, steps, policy, validation}}`; `alerts:[8 {tool, text}]`; `teams:[6]`; and, for the security mission, `security {verdict, tactics:[5], story:[5], responses:[4]}`.

**Facilities** (`facilities[siteId]`): `title, entity, address, intro` (spoken), `context` (manhattan|tokyo|cdmx|santiago|dubai|noida|brighton|campus), `buildings:[{id, label, shape: rect|octagon|faceted|datacenter, w, d, floors, floorH, x, z, rot?, podium?, metlife?:[[from,to]] customer floors, heightVerified?}]`, optional `landmarks, parking, lake, ponds, trees, mountains`, `facts:[4-5 {k, v, verified}]`, text-only `sources`, `links:[2-3 {to, label, bearing}]`.

**Zones** (`zones[missionId]`): `{buildingId, floor, room, basis, verified, devices: 4-5 {kind, label}}`. The basis states what is public and what is illustrative.

**Opening tour:** 6 chapters `{title, short, text, cam:{lat,lon,dist}, layer}`: customer promise (`sites`), strategy numbers (`sites`), "The era of network operations is changing" (`silos`), "One fabric of data" (`fabric`), "A vantage point above it all" (`agents`), "From IT problems to business outcomes" (`all`).

Also write a `finale` paragraph, 20 `ticker` lines ("City | Agent did X. Outcome."), 8 badges, 5 ranks and 22 or so `sites` (the mission hubs plus minor offices).

**Copy rules:** Plain, confident English. No em dashes. Mission titles are 2 to 5 words. Every dollar figure is labelled as modeled.

## 5. Data schema

One `src/data/content.json` with `sites, lenses, tour, finale, ranks, badges, missions, facilities, zones, views, ticker, lanes, fabricSources, fabricActions, studioVoices, strings`, shaped as in section 4. The 5 `lanes` are ThousandEyes `#38c6f4`, Splunk Data Fabric `#f99d1c`, Cloud Control agents `#5191f0`, Security XDR `#ff6a8a`, People and business `#a4ce4e`; events map to lanes by regex on `source`.

## 6. Layout (1440x900 reference)

- **Full-bleed WebGL globe** behind everything. Keep it centred in the free space between the side panels with `camera.setViewOffset`.
- **Top bar, 56px:** Cisco bars logo with "{{CUSTOMER}} x Cisco Cloud Control" / "AgenticOps 4D · modeled scenarios"; mode tabs (Executive Tour | Explore Missions | Academy); live vantage stats (signals/hr, agents, resolved today); green score "VALUE PROTECTED · MODELED"; rank with XP bar; Badges (count), Voice, Ambient.
- **Breadcrumb pill**, centred under the bar: Globe › Region › City › Campus › Building › Floor N (room). Every crumb drills the camera.
- **Left mission rail, about 300px glass:** "Missions", lens chips ("All functions" plus one per function with a colour dot), mission rows (code tile, title, "City | Unit", 3 lens bars, status: Not started / Protected / Partial / Impacted with "$X at stake" or "$X" and "Quiz N%"), footer "Replay the opening".
- **Right step panel, about 384px glass:** kicker "M-01 | City, Country", title, subtitle, lens tags, step chips, scrolling body, "Live agent log" (events up to the playhead, newest first), nav row Back / Pause / Overview / Next (Next pulses on manual steps).
- **Bottom stack:** the 4D timeline (about 150 to 200px), then the live ticker (26px), then the audio dock (50px, max 900px, centred).
- **Stage windows:** floating product panels that dock into slots (nw, ne, sw, se, w, e, n, s, center) between the rails, with a dashed animated leader line to the site.
- **Captions:** centred above the timeline.
- **Mobile (≤760px):** tabs wrap to their own row, the rail becomes a "Missions" drawer, the step panel a 42vh bottom sheet; hide timeline, ticker and captions; one stage window at a time; intro cards stack; no horizontal scroll.

## 7. Design tokens

- **Background `#02050c`.** Glass `rgba(6,14,30,.74)` with a 14px blur; lines `rgba(120,170,255,.16)` and `.30`.
- **Text:** ink `#e6f0ff`, ink-2 `#c7d4ea`, muted `#93a7c6`, dim `#6b7f9f`.
- **Accents:** Cisco blue `#049fd9`, sky `#3fb6ff`, cyan `#7fe7ff`, fabric `#2fb4ff`.
- **States:** signal `#ffd166`, warning `#ffb020`, critical `#ff3b4f`, recovering `#ff9f43`, protected `#7cf29c`.
- **Timeline:** traditional `#ff4d5e`, AgenticOps `#6ff09a`, forecast `#ffc14d`.
- **Lenses:** revenue `#a4ce4e`, customer `#5ec8f2`, operations `#f2c14e`, risk `#c792ea`, security `#ff6b6b`, IT `#049fd9`.
- **Academy chain:** signal `#00bceb`, domain `#8e7cff`, capability `#2de2c5`, KPI `#fbab18`, outcome `#6cc04a`.
- **Radii:** 14 panels, 10 buttons, 999 chips.
- **Type:** panel title 19px/760, lead 14px, body 13px, uppercase micro-labels 10.5px with 0.12em letter-spacing, window text 11.5px. Use tabular numbers.
- **Intro:** kicker 13px/800, 0.3em tracking, customer name sky blue; H1 `clamp(32px, 4.4vw, 64px)`/800 with gradient `#f2fbff → #c4ecff → #8fe3d9 → #a6d977`; lead 18px `#9fb2cf` with product names bold white; three glass cards (11px cyan kicker, 22px title, 14px muted text).

## 8. Globe

- **Renderer:** ACES filmic tone mapping, exposure 1.05, clear colour `#02050c`. UnrealBloom at strength 0.62, radius 0.5, threshold 0.32, then an OutputPass. Labels use CSS2D.
- **Ocean:** a fresnel sphere of radius 0.995.
- **Land:** about 95,000 Fibonacci-sphere points, kept where a 2048x1024 canvas raster of the TopoJSON land says land (latitude ≥ -62°).
- **Point shader:** day/night from a sun that follows the mission clock (`lon = siteLon + 30 - hours × 15`), amber city lights on about 3.5% of night points, and uniforms for a focus glow, a scan ring and a rippling incident disc (red, amber or green).
- **Atmosphere:** a back-face additive shell at 1.16× in `#1d8fff`. Add 2,600 stars.
- **Vantage shell (Cloud Control):** icosahedron wireframe (r 1.55, detail 3, about 5% opacity), three tilted counter-rotating torus rings, nine glowing octahedron "agents" orbiting them.
- **Data streams:** 26 particles per site rise to the shell. In the "silos" layer they take siloed colours and stop short.
- **Fabric arcs:** about 30 great-circle tubes between sites, with lift `0.03 + min(d, 1.3) × 0.17` and a travelling pulse head in `#2fb4ff`.
- **Pins:** spike (hubs 2× taller), glow head, base and pulse rings, protected dome, hit sphere; colour tweens by state; CSS2D label with city and live note ("T-48h 00m | Agent acting"); click opens the mission, hover shows a tooltip.
- **Blast radius:** red arcs from the mission site to its `blast` sites while the state is critical.
- **Agent beam and shockwave:** a striped cyan beam on the site while the agent acts (one shell agent flies to it). A green shockwave ring when the site becomes protected.
- **Ambient flashes:** a random green or cyan flash every 1.3 s.
- **Story layers** tween 5 values (fabric, streams, reach, silo, shell) over 2.2 s, with presets `sites`, `silos`, `fabric`, `agents` and `all`.
- **Camera:** FOV 42, start at lat 25, lon -40, distance 3.8 with idle spin; `flyTo(lat, lon, dist)` on a great circle with mid-flight lift; region 3.25, city 2.2 at lat - 6, branch views 3.1 / 2.35; orbit controls, no pan, 1.35 to 7.
- **Building close-up** (fly to 1.32, radial "warp" flash, second scene): shader street grid with radar ring; procedural lit-window city in the site's `context` style; landmarks, water, trees; the real building(s) as translucent floor slabs, customer floors blue, mission floor cyan coloured by state, hover tooltips (public vs illustrative).
- **Floor focus:** fade upper floors, dim the city, reveal desks, a room box and labelled device beacons. Warning beam, red critical alarm ring, green protected dome. Drill: globe › region › city › site › building › floor.

## 9. Mode flows

Each mode is a list of steps. A step has `narration`, `enter()` (camera, timeline and drill), `render()` (HTML for the right panel), `cues: [[fraction, fn]]` that fire as narration progresses, and `wait: 'auto' | 'manual'` (auto advances 1.4 s after the narration ends).

- **Intro screen** over the spinning globe: kicker, {{HEADLINE}} as H1, lead, three cards (PRESENT · Executive Tour, PLAY · Explore Missions, LEARN · Account Team Academy), disclaimer, "Best with sound on…". Support `?mode=…&mission=<id>&voice=off`.
- **Executive Tour** (narrated, auto-advancing): 6 opening chapters; per mission Briefing (into the building, then the floor), Signal, Timeline A, Timeline B, Outcome; a finale with all sites protected, the total modeled value, a value table, and Explore / Academy buttons.
- **Explore Missions.** The idle panel reads "Choose a mission". The steps are:
  1. Overview (audio overview and chain).
  2. Briefing (cards: where it happens, known industry challenge, strategy priority at stake, Data Fabric sources joined).
  3. Signal (play the AgenticOps view to 30% of the agent window; ThousandEyes path, Splunk ITSI and AI Assistant windows; lead-time callout).
  4. **Decision**, manual. The AI Canvas shows the proposed action and "Your call"; the same options appear in the right panel; Next is disabled until a choice is made.
  5. Your outcome. Best plays the AgenticOps branch; partial or poor plays the traditional branch.
  6. The other timeline.
  7. Outcome, manual: a big modeled number, the basis, the KPI table, the chain and the products, with buttons Next mission, Replay and make a better call, and All missions.
- **Account Team Academy.** Overview, Briefing, Signal, Timeline A, Timeline B, Outcome, then:
  - **Connections:** a big chain, talk track, "Discovery questions to ask" and capability chips;
  - **Quiz:** answer to reveal; the score earns XP; then Next mission.
- **Stage windows** (opened by cues and timeline clicks): Splunk ITSI health and service tree; ThousandEyes path with bad hop and alternate; AI Canvas (typed prompt, 4-agent plan, forecast, root cause, policy-checked action, Approve / Revise / Reject, "Your call", reasoning trail); AI Assistant with generated SPL2 and follow-ups; the traditional "12 tools, 6 teams, 1 bridge call" storm; XDR attack story with SOAR tasks; Business impact (Modeled); Facility facts; Data Fabric diagram; Cloud Control topology. The tour adds five context panels.
- **Keys:** Space pauses. Left / Right moves by sentence. Shift + arrows or PgUp/PgDn move by section. Escape closes.

## 10. 4D timeline

- **Model.** One mission clock in hours or minutes from T-0. Branches are `traditional` and `agentic`; views are Compare, Traditional and AgenticOps.
- **KPI health (0 to 100):** traditional dips by `tradDip` from T-0 to `tradRecover`; agentic dips by `agentDip` between detect and remediate, then improves slightly; small jitter on both.
- **Site state** drives globe, building and windows: traditional idle › signal › critical › recovering › idle; agentic idle › warning › protected.
- **Canvas chart:** 132px label gutter, KPI band in the top 40% (grid 0/50/100), 5 swim lanes, dashed T-0 "business moment" line, glowing curves (dashed forecast in the AgenticOps view), event diamonds (agentic) and circles (traditional, white ring if critical), lead-time and outage bands, white playhead, "Agent lead time: N hours".
- **Interaction.** Drag to scrub. Hover an event for a tooltip; click it to open the matching window and toast the event. The header shows the clock `T-48h 00m`, KPI read-outs and "Exposure $X (modeled)". There is a Hide button.

## 11. Game logic

- **Value protected** = `exposure × {best: 1, partial: 0.4, poor: 0}`. Keep only the best result per mission. Tour and academy runs count as best.
- **XP:** +150 / +60 / +20 per outcome quality; +20 the first time a mission's timelines are compared; +30 per correct quiz answer.
- **Ranks:** Observer 0, Operator 200, Correlator 600, Orchestrator 1200, AgenticOps Architect 2000.
- **8 badges:** First Save, Perfect Call (3 best calls), Americas / Asia / EMEA Guardian (all missions in a region), Account Scholar (100% on 3 quizzes), Time Traveler (compare in 5 missions), Global Vantage (all missions).
- **Rewards:** a toast plus a chime, and a floating "+XP +$X". There is a badges modal with a reset.
- **Persistence:** `localStorage` with `{{CUSTOMER_SLUG}}-agenticops-*` keys, wrapped in try/catch.
- **WebAudio:** an ambient pad (off by default; it ducks under narration), and cues for info, warn, crit, good and badge. Create the AudioContext only after a user gesture.

## 12. Narration

- **Sentence engine.** Split narration into sentences. Speak them one at a time, fire step cues by `(index + sentenceProgress) / total`, and show each sentence as a caption.
- **Dock:** section and sentence skip, play/pause, a clickable segment bar (one segment per sentence, width by length, live fill), counter, and a voice popover (Voice and Captions toggles, speed 0.85 to 1.5x, Studio / Premium device / Other device voices with previews). Settings persist.
- **Studio voices:** Heart, Michael (US English), Emma, George (British English) at `audio/<voice>/<fnv1a32(collapsed sentence)>.mp3`; manifest in `<script type="application/json" id="studio-manifest">` (`{"base":"audio","voices":{}}` when empty); `tools/narration-lines.mjs` prints `{hash, text}` per sentence for offline rendering.
- **Fallback per sentence:** studio MP3 if listed, else the best English `speechSynthesis` voice (prefer natural / neural / premium / enhanced / online / google / siri names), else a silent timer of `words / 2.6 / rate + 0.5` s. Drop a failing MP3 hash and retry; on an autoplay block, toast and resume on the next gesture. Nothing may throw without audio.

## 13. Disclaimer

Show this verbatim on the intro, filled in: "Illustrative scenarios built from public information about {{CUSTOMER}} (including {{STRATEGY}} and public filings) and common challenges across the {{INDUSTRY}} industry. No {{CUSTOMER}} internal data is used. Dollar figures are modeled estimates based on industry benchmarks, meant for discussion only."

Label the score, timeline exposure and impact window "modeled", show each outcome's "Modeled:" basis, tag facility facts "Public source" or "Illustrative", and add no source links in the UI.

## 14. Quality checks and review

- **Content:** all fields present; detect < remediate < 0 < tradDetect < tradRecover; narration uses only facts in the data; no em dashes; every dollar labelled modeled.
- **Playwright review** (Chromium, `--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`) at 1280x720 and 1440x900: intro, Explore idle, a Decision step, Academy Connections, an AgenticOps timeline; plus intro and a mission at 390x844.
- **Pass criteria:** zero console errors; no mobile horizontal overflow; a decision updates score, XP, rail and badges; the quiz scores; scrubbing changes globe states; the tour auto-advances with `?voice=off`.
- Do 2 or 3 visual passes: fix overlap, crowding at 1280x720, legibility of the timeline lanes, and panel scroll.

## 15. Deliverables

1. `dist/{{CUSTOMER_SLUG}}.html`, a single self-contained file of about 1 to 1.5 MB, plus an empty `dist/audio/`.
2. The `app/` source with `npm run build`.
3. `research.md` with the source for each fact and each value basis.
4. Screenshots of the review states.
5. README notes: adding studio voices, deep links, editing `content.json`.
